overall: A plain, curious and dry narrator who has followed this restaurant story and is telling the viewer the one thing to keep: software took the order, and the tip rests on the owner's word. Curious at the question, brisk and easy through the order, dry at the money and the rule, and level and certain at the close. Never triumphant, because every dollar figure and the tip claim are the owner's account.
performance_arc: Curiosity at the question, discovery at the host, consequence at the money and the rule, and a level answer at the close.

lines.emphasis: who was going to take the order

audit.picture_check: The closing tag reads no record shown. That label is not spoken and does not replace a spoken claim.

text:
When the only server at Wok and Karahi in Spring walked out, who was going to take the order?
The family didn't post a job ad. They put an AI host named Haniya at the front of the house.
A guest scans a code at the table, taps or talks to order, and pays from a phone.
Nothing is cooked until the order is paid for.
The owner says the restaurant saves or wins back $9,650 a month, and that's his own count.
FOX 26 reports that kitchen staff now get all of the tips.
When the employer takes no tip credit, federal rules allow a tip pool with cooks.
No report says whether this restaurant takes one.
One customer said QR codes don't suit people like her mother.
So software now takes the order, and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.
